questions.question: Which structures within plant leaf cells are responsible for carrying out photosynthesis?
options: Mitochondria
Chloroplasts
Vacuoles
Ribosomes

questions.question: Where precisely does the process of photosynthesis take place inside a plant cell?
options: In the cytoplasm
In the nucleus
In the chloroplasts
In the cell wall

questions.question: What is the function of chlorophyll found inside chloroplasts?
options: To absorb light energy for photosynthesis
To absorb water from the soil
To release carbon dioxide into the air
To store glucose molecules

questions.question: How does the thinness of a plant leaf help it perform photosynthesis efficiently?
options: It prevents water from evaporating too quickly
It allows light to easily pass through to the chloroplast-containing cells
It makes the leaf lighter so it can float on water
It stops insects from eating the plant cells

questions.question: What is the main advantage of plant leaves having a large surface area?
options: To maximize the absorption of light for photosynthesis
To store extra water during dry periods
To protect the plant from strong winds
To increase the rate of mineral absorption from soil

questions.question: Which gas do plant leaves take in from the surrounding air to use in photosynthesis?
options: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen

questions.question: What gas is produced during photosynthesis and released from the leaves into the air?
options: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Water vapour
Nitrogen

questions.question: What are the small holes on the surface of leaves that allow gas exchange to happen?
options: Pores
Stomata
Chloroplasts
Veins

questions.question: By which process do gas molecules move into and out of the leaf through open stomata?
options: Osmosis
Active transport
Diffusion
Transpiration

questions.question: Under which condition can the process of photosynthesis take place?
options: Only in complete darkness
Only when there is light
Only when the plant is submerged in water
At any time, regardless of light levels

questions.question: What are the chemical reactants required for photosynthesis, and what are its products?
options: Reactants: oxygen and glucose; Products: water and carbon dioxide
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose
Reactants: oxygen and water; Products: carbon dioxide and glucose
Reactants: carbon dioxide and glucose; Products: oxygen and water

questions.question: How do plants obtain the water and minerals they need to stay alive?
options: They absorb them from the air through their leaves
They absorb them from the soil through their roots
They produce them inside their chloroplasts
They take them in from sunlight

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding water, minerals, and plant nutrition?
options: Water and minerals are the food that plants eat
Plants do not need water or minerals to survive
Water and minerals are not food, but plants still need them to stay alive and grow
Water and minerals are converted directly into light energy

questions.question: Why are plants classified as producers?
options: Because they take in food from their surroundings
Because they make their own food instead of taking it in from their surroundings
Because they produce carbon dioxide for other animals to breathe
Because they decay and produce soil minerals

questions.question: What type of food do plants produce during photosynthesis, and what do they use it for?
options: Proteins, used to build cell walls
Fats, used for long-term water storage
Carbohydrate, used for growth and as a source of energy
Minerals, used to strengthen the stem
